subject: maths
note: Partial bank: only questions on G12 Maths Unit 1 (sequences and series) and Unit 2 (calculus). EUEE Mathematics for Natural Science, Yekatit 2013 E.C. (printed '2012/13; March 2020/21'), booklet 48 — key-p1.pdf pp. 208–215, solutions pp. 216–232

items.text: A geometric series with first term a and common ratio r is convergent if
items.why:
1) The geometric series a + ar + ar² + … has partial sums S_n = a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r) for r ≠ 1.
2) rⁿ → 0 exactly when |r| < 1, i.e. −1 < r < 1; then S_n → a/(1 − r).
3) If |r| ≥ 1 (and a ≠ 0) the terms do not tend to 0, so the series diverges.
4) A, B are wrong (r ≥ 1 diverges). C includes r = 1 and all r ≤ −1, which diverge. D 'r < 1' wrongly includes r ≤ −1 (e.g. r = −2 gives 1 − 2 + 4 − 8 + … , divergent).
5) The correct condition |r| < 1 is not among the options; D is the closest but is incomplete.
items.review: The book marks 'No Answer'. Agreed: the correct condition is |r| < 1 (−1 < r < 1); option D 'r < 1' is incomplete. If one option must be chosen, D is the intended one.

items.text: Which one of the following is an upper bound of the sequence {(n+1)/n}_{n=1}^∞?
items.why:
1) Write a_n = (n+1)/n = 1 + 1/n.
2) For n ≥ 1, 0 < 1/n ≤ 1, so 1 < a_n ≤ 2. Terms: 2, 3/2, 4/3, 5/4, … (decreasing).
3) An upper bound M must satisfy a_n ≤ M for every n; the largest term is a_1 = 2, so any M ≥ 2 works.
4) 1 and 0 are below every term; 4/3 < a_1 = 2 and < a_2 = 3/2. Only 2 is an upper bound.

items.text: The general term of a sequence is given by a_n = (1/2)^(1−n). Then, which one of the following is true about this sequence?
opts: A. 0 is one of its terms.
C. Its terms are odd numbers.
D. Its terms are natural numbers.
items.why:
1) (1/2)^(1−n) = 2^(n−1).
2) Terms for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …
3) All terms are positive (so A and B are false), they include even numbers (so C is false), and every term is a natural number (D true).

items.text: Given 0 < a_n < 1/n for each n = 1, 2, 3, …, which one of the following is true?
opts: C. lim_{n→∞} a_n does not exist
items.why:
1) We have 0 < a_n < 1/n for all n.
2) lim 0 = 0 and lim_{n→∞} 1/n = 0.
3) By the sandwich (squeeze) theorem, lim_{n→∞} a_n = 0.
4) So the limit exists (C false) and is neither negative (A) nor positive (D).
topics: limit of a sequence, sandwich theorem

items.text: Let f(x) = x² + 2x + 3. For what number c ∈ (1, 3) is f′(c) = (f(3) − f(1))/2?
For what value of c is the conclusion of Rolle's Theorem satisfied for the function f(x) = 2x − x² − x³ on [−2, 1]?
The second derivative of the function f(x) = xe^(−x) is ____.
The volume of a cube is increasing at a rate of 9 cm³/sec. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of the edge is 10 cm?
items.why:
1) Edge x, V = x³, A = 6x².
2) dV/dt = 3x² dx/dt ⇒ 9 = 3(10)² dx/dt ⇒ dx/dt = 9/300 = 0.03 cm/s.
3) dA/dt = 12x dx/dt = 12(10)(0.03) = 3.6 cm²/s.
4) Shortcut: dA/dt = (4/x)·dV/dt = (4/10)(9) = 3.6. ✓

items.text: The product of two positive numbers is 100 such that the sum of two times the first number and eight times the second number is minimum. Which one of the following pairs of numbers are the first and the second numbers respectively?
items.why:
1) Let the numbers be x, y > 0 with xy = 100, so y = 100/x.
2) S(x) = 2x + 8y = 2x + 800/x.
3) S′(x) = 2 − 800/x² = 0 ⇒ x² = 400 ⇒ x = 20 (x > 0); y = 100/20 = 5.
4) S″(x) = 1600/x³ > 0, so this is a minimum: S = 40 + 40 = 80.
5) Check others: (25,4) gives 82, (50,2) gives 116; (1,99) has product 99, not 100.

items.text: The maximum profit that a company can make if the profit function is given by P(x) = 36 + 72x − 18x² is ____.
If the 1st and 4th terms of a geometric progression are 3 and 81 respectively, what is the common ratio of this progression?
Which one of the following is an interval at which the function f(x) = 1/(x − 1) − √(4 − x²) is differentiable?
items.why:
1) f′(x) = −1/(x − 1)² + x/√(4 − x²).
2) f′ needs x ≠ 1 and 4 − x² > 0, i.e. −2 < x < 2 (at x = ±2 the square-root term has a vertical tangent, so no derivative).
3) So f is differentiable on (−2, 1) ∪ (1, 2).
4) B includes x = 1 (f undefined); C lies outside the domain; D includes the endpoints ±2.

items.text: The function f(x) = (x − 1)^(2/3) is differentiable on:
items.why:
1) f′(x) = (2/3)(x − 1)^(−1/3) = 2/(3·∛(x − 1)).
2) This is undefined only at x = 1 (cusp of the graph).
3) So f is differentiable on ℝ \ {1} = (−∞, 1) ∪ (1, ∞).

items.text: What is the slope of the line tangent to the graph of f(x) = x² + tan x at a point (π, f(π))?
items.why:
1) f′(x) = 2x + sec²x.
2) sec π = 1/cos π = −1, so sec²π = 1.
3) Slope = f′(π) = 2π + 1.

items.text: If f(x) = 4 − x² sin x, then which one of the following expressions describes f′(x)?
opts: C. x(x cos x − 2 sin x)
items.why:
1) d/dx(4) = 0.
2) Product rule: d/dx(x² sin x) = 2x sin x + x² cos x.
3) f′(x) = −(2x sin x + x² cos x) = −x(x cos x + 2 sin x).

topics: recursive sequence, sum of geometric series

items.text: Let f(x) = 1/(1 − √x)². Then, f′(4) is equal to ____.
items.review: Book key A (1/2) is wrong. The book writes f′ = −(g²)′/g⁴ and then drops the minus sign in the next line, getting +1/2. Correct value f′(4) = −1/2 (option B), confirmed by a numerical difference quotient.

items.text: Given the function f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, what is the slope of the line passing through the points (−1, f(−1)) and (2, f(2))?
topics: average rate of change, slope of secant line
items.review: Options A and D are both printed as −1 in the book; the value −1 is correct (book key D).

items.text: A real number a is the limit of a sequence {a_n} if
opts: A. a is closer to every term of the sequence.
C. a is very close to all terms a_n from some arbitrary big n onwards.
items.why:
1) lim a_n = a means: for every ε > 0 there is N such that |a_n − a| < ε for all n ≥ N.
2) In words: from some (large) n onwards, all terms are as close to a as we like — option C.
3) A is vague and not the definition; B and D are inequalities about size, not closeness (e.g. a_n = 1/n → 0 but D fails for many sequences).

items.text: Which one of the following is equal to lim_{n→∞} sin n / n²?
items.why:
1) −1 ≤ sin n ≤ 1, so −1/n² ≤ sin n / n² ≤ 1/n².
2) lim −1/n² = 0 = lim 1/n².
3) By the squeeze theorem, lim_{n→∞} sin n / n² = 0.
topics: limit of a sequence, squeeze theorem

items.text: If f(x) = ln 2 / x², then f′(x) is equal to
items.why:
1) ln 2 is a constant, so f(x) = (ln 2)·x^(−2).
2) f′(x) = (ln 2)(−2)x^(−3) = −2 ln 2 / x³.
3) Common error: treating ln 2 as a function of x (it is a number ≈ 0.693).

items.text: What is the slope of the line tangent to the graph of f(x) = x² + tan x at (π, f(π))?
items.why:
1) Same item as Q30 (repeated in the paper).
2) f′(x) = 2x + sec²x; sec²π = 1.
3) Slope = f′(π) = 2π + 1.

items.text: Let {a_n} be a sequence of real numbers. Then, which one of the following is true about this sequence?
opts: A. M is an upper bound of {a_n} if M ≤ a_n for all a_n.
B. m is a lower bound of {a_n} if a_n ≤ m for all a_n.
C. The sequence {a_n} is bounded if it has both an upper and a lower bound.
D. The sequence {a_n} is bounded if there exists k > 0 such that k ≤ |a_n| for all a_n.
items.why:
1) M is an upper bound if a_n ≤ M for all n (A has the inequality reversed).
2) m is a lower bound if a_n ≥ m for all n (B reversed).
3) Bounded means bounded above and below — C is true.
4) Bounded is equivalent to |a_n| ≤ k for some k > 0; D has the inequality reversed.

items.text: Which of the following is a lower bound for the sequence {n/(n − 1)}_{n=2}^∞?
items.why:
1) a_n = n/(n − 1) = 1 + 1/(n − 1).
2) Terms: 2, 3/2, 4/3, 5/4, … decreasing towards 1, and every a_n > 1.
3) A lower bound m needs m ≤ a_n for all n; since a_n gets arbitrarily close to 1, m must be ≤ 1.
4) 9/5, 7/4 and 5/3 are larger than a_3 = 3/2, so they fail. Only 1 works.
